avoid_list.selection: A double-digit-leg NFL moneyline mega-parlay stacking this week's favorites (e.g. Ravens/Bucs/49ers/Seahawks/Eagles/Packers/Cowboys/Broncos MLs all on one ticket)
avoid_list.why_tempting: Stacking 8-10 real favorites together produces a huge payout number, and each individual leg looks 'safe' on its own -- it's exactly the shape of Gus's real Sept 13 10-leg SGPx parlay (PIT/CIN/BAL/CHI/BUF/TEN MLs + two 2-pick SGPs, +9164 boosted to +13748).
avoid_list.why_avoid: That real Sept 13 ticket lost, and the math explains why: even at 70-85% per leg, 8-10 legs multiplied together lands the combined probability in single-digit territory. This is Rule 4's whole point -- leg count has to follow probability, and double-digit legs never clear that bar no matter how good each individual pick is.

avoid_list.why_tempting: Falcons are the designated spread favorite at -1.5/-110, which reads as the lower-variance side of a close game.
avoid_list.why_avoid: Two things undercut that read: Atlanta's own Kalshi win probability (50%) is actually a hair BELOW Carolina's (52%), despite Atlanta being the spread favorite -- a genuine model/market disagreement, not noise. avoid_list.selection: Building a parlay specifically to clear DraftKings' '+100 or longer' threshold for the standing 50% profit-boost token (e.g. stacking Titans/Cardinals/Colts/Jets/Browns underdogs)
avoid_list.why_tempting: The boost token is real and currently active, and it feels like leaving free value on the table if this week's card doesn't use it.

Every underdog that would be needed to reach +100 graded poorly in the real research this week (Titans 25% Kalshi win prob, Cardinals 17%, etc.) -- building a parlay around bad picks just to hit a boost's odds floor is boost-first construction, exactly the trap Rule 3 exists to prevent.
